A method, device, and computer program are provided in which the method comprises receiving three or more ambient audio signals. At least one of these signals is processed using a first pair of directional transfer functions, while at least one different ambient audio signal is processed using a second pair of directional transfer functions. The particular directional transfer function pairs applied are chosen according to the target directions of the ambient audio signals.

The method further includes identifying that the target direction of the at least one ambient audio signal has changed to a revised target direction. An updated pair of directional transfer functions corresponding to the revised target direction is then chosen from among multiple available directional transfer functions. This updated pair is selected because it corresponds more closely to the revised target direction than the first directional transfer function pair. The at least one ambient audio signal is then processed using the selected updated directional transfer function pair, while the other ambient audio signal continues to be processed using the second directional transfer function pair.
outputs.L3:
The method obtains at least three ambient audio signals for use in directional audio processing. Each ambient audio signal may correspond to sound captured from, or intended to be rendered as coming from, a particular target direction within an audio environment.

The method processes different ambient audio signals using respective directional transfer function pairs. Each directional transfer function pair is selected based on the target direction associated with the corresponding ambient audio signal. For example, a first ambient audio signal may be processed using a first directional transfer function pair that represents a first target direction, while a second ambient audio signal may be processed using a second directional transfer function pair that represents a different target direction.

During operation, the method determines whether the target direction of at least one of the ambient audio signals has changed. When a change is detected, the method identifies an updated target direction for that ambient audio signal. The updated target direction may reflect movement of a sound source, movement of a listener, a change in spatial rendering parameters, or another modification to the intended spatial position of the audio signal.

In response to determining the updated target direction, the method selects an updated directional transfer function pair from a plurality of available directional transfer function pairs. The selected updated directional transfer function pair is chosen to more closely correspond to the updated target direction than the previously used directional transfer function pair.

The ambient audio signal whose target direction has changed is then processed using the updated directional transfer function pair. At the same time, at least one other ambient audio signal continues to be processed using its original directional transfer function pair, because its target direction has not changed. In this way, the method allows directional audio processing to be dynamically updated for selected ambient audio signals while maintaining stable processing for other ambient audio signals.
outputs.L4:
The method relates to the spatial processing of a plurality of ambient audio signals, such as signals captured by multiple microphones or generated as separate ambient sound components in an audio scene. Each ambient audio signal is associated with a target direction that represents the perceived or intended direction from which that signal should be rendered to a listener. To reproduce the signals spatially, the method assigns to each signal a corresponding pair of directional transfer functions, such as a left-ear and right-ear transfer function pair. These transfer functions may be selected from a stored set of transfer function pairs, with each pair corresponding to a particular direction or range of directions.

During operation, each ambient audio signal is processed using the transfer function pair assigned to its target direction. The processed signals may then be combined to produce a spatial audio output, for example a binaural output for headphone playback or another format suitable for spatial rendering. Because different signals may have different target directions, different transfer function pairs may be assigned to different signals at the same time. This allows the system to preserve the spatial characteristics of each signal within the overall sound field.

The method further includes monitoring whether the target direction of any ambient audio signal changes. A target direction may change, for example, when a virtual sound source moves, when a listener’s head orientation changes, when scene metadata is updated, or when the spatial position of an ambient component is recalculated. When such a change is detected for one of the signals, the system determines whether the transfer function pair currently assigned to that signal remains appropriate for the updated direction. If a different available transfer function pair more closely corresponds to the updated target direction, the system assigns that new pair to the affected signal.

The other ambient audio signals can continue to be processed using their previously assigned transfer function pairs unless their own target directions also change. In this way, the method avoids unnecessarily recalculating or reassigning transfer functions for every signal whenever only one signal’s direction is updated. This can reduce processing complexity while maintaining accurate spatial placement of individual audio components.

By selecting a transfer function pair that more closely matches the updated target direction, the method improves the perceived directional accuracy of the rendered audio. As a result, sound components can be positioned more precisely within the listener’s perceived environment, producing a more natural and immersive spatial audio experience. The approach is particularly useful in applications such as virtual reality, augmented reality, gaming, teleconferencing, cinematic audio, and other systems in which accurate and dynamically updated spatial sound rendering is desirable.

counterfactuals.output: An audio processing system and method are provided for generating a spatially enhanced audio output from a plurality of ambient audio signals. The system receives multiple ambient audio input signals captured by one or more microphones and processes the signals using a plurality of directional transfer function pairs associated with respective target directions. A selected directional transfer function pair is applied to the ambient audio signals to produce left and right output signals having a perceived spatial direction corresponding to a current target direction. In response to detecting a change in the target direction, the system updates the selected directional transfer function pair to a different pair corresponding to the changed target direction. The updated transfer function pair is then applied to subsequently received ambient audio signals, thereby maintaining spatial correspondence between the generated audio output and the target direction. The directional transfer function pairs may comprise head-related, binaural, or other spatial transfer functions and may be selected, interpolated, or dynamically adapted based on the changed target direction.

Below is example patent-style language describing spatial audio rendering in which different ambient audio signals are processed using different directional transfer function pairs, including selecting a closer matching pair after an updated target direction is determined.

---

## Example Specification Language

In some implementations, an audio rendering system is configured to render a plurality of ambient audio signals as spatial audio. The plurality of ambient audio signals may correspond to environmental, background, reverberant, diffuse, or otherwise non-primary audio components associated with a virtual, augmented, mixed-reality, gaming, teleconferencing, media playback, or other immersive audio scene.

The system may store, access, or generate a plurality of directional transfer function pairs. Each directional transfer function pair may include a first transfer function associated with a first ear or first output channel and a second transfer function associated with a second ear or second output channel. In some examples, the directional transfer function pairs comprise head-related transfer function pairs, binaural room impulse response pairs, spatial filter pairs, personalized transfer function pairs, generalized transfer function pairs, or any combination thereof. Each directional transfer function pair may be associated with a corresponding direction, location, angular region, sector, elevation, azimuth, distance, or other spatial parameter.

Different ambient audio signals may be processed using different directional transfer function pairs. For example, a first ambient audio signal may be rendered using a first directional transfer function pair associated with a first target direction, and a second ambient audio signal may be rendered using a second directional transfer function pair associated with a second target direction different from the first target direction. The resulting processed signals may be combined to generate left and right binaural output signals, multichannel output signals, or other spatialized audio output signals.

In some implementations, a target direction for an ambient audio signal may be determined based on metadata, object position information, scene geometry, listener pose, head orientation, camera pose, acoustic analysis, ambience classification, random or pseudo-random distribution, room simulation parameters, or other spatial rendering information. The target direction may be updated over time, for example in response to movement of a listener, movement of a sound source, a change in a virtual scene, a change in an acoustic environment, or a change in rendering parameters.

After an updated target direction is determined for an ambient audio signal, the system may select a directional transfer function pair that more closely matches the updated target direction than a previously selected directional transfer function pair. For instance, the system may compare the updated target direction with respective directions associated with a plurality of available directional transfer function pairs and select a closest matching pair based on an angular distance, a weighted angular distance, an interpolation criterion, a psychoacoustic metric, a perceptual error metric, a distance metric in a spherical coordinate space, or another matching criterion.

In some implementations, the system may replace a previously selected directional transfer function pair with the closer matching directional transfer function pair. In other implementations, the system may transition between the previously selected directional transfer function pair and the closer matching directional transfer function pair using interpolation, crossfading, smoothing, filtering, hysteresis, or another temporal transition technique to reduce audible artifacts. The updated directional transfer function pair may then be applied to the ambient audio signal to generate an updated spatialized representation of the ambient audio signal.

The system may process different ambient audio signals independently such that, at a given time, different ambient audio signals are convolved, filtered, or otherwise transformed using different respective directional transfer function pairs. The processed ambient audio signals may be summed, mixed, encoded, or otherwise combined with one another and optionally with one or more direct audio signals, object audio signals, channel audio signals, or reverberant audio signals to produce a spatial audio output.

---

## Example Method Claim

1. A method of rendering spatial audio, the method comprising:  
   receiving a plurality of ambient audio signals;  
   determining, for a first ambient audio signal of the plurality of ambient audio signals, a first target direction;  
   selecting, from a plurality of directional transfer function pairs, a first directional transfer function pair corresponding to the first target direction;  
   processing the first ambient audio signal using the first directional transfer function pair;  
   determining, for a second ambient audio signal of the plurality of ambient audio signals, a second target direction different from the first target direction;  
   selecting, from the plurality of directional transfer function pairs, a second directional transfer function pair corresponding to the second target direction, the second directional transfer function pair being different from the first directional transfer function pair;  
   processing the second ambient audio signal using the second directional transfer function pair;  
   determining an updated target direction for at least one of the first ambient audio signal or the second ambient audio signal;  
   selecting, after determining the updated target direction, a closer matching directional transfer function pair from the plurality of directional transfer function pairs based on the updated target direction; and  
   rendering an output spatial audio signal based at least in part on the first ambient audio signal processed using the first directional transfer function pair, the second ambient audio signal processed using the second directional transfer function pair, and the at least one ambient audio signal processed using the closer matching directional transfer function pair.

---

## Example Dependent Claims

2. The method of claim 1, wherein each directional transfer function pair comprises a left-ear transfer function and a right-ear transfer function.

3. The method of claim 1, wherein the plurality of directional transfer function pairs comprises a plurality of head-related transfer function pairs associated with different azimuth and elevation values.

4. The method of claim 1, wherein selecting the closer matching directional transfer function pair comprises determining an angular distance between the updated target direction and a direction associated with each of at least a subset of the plurality of directional transfer function pairs.

5. The method of claim 4, wherein the closer matching directional transfer function pair is associated with a direction having a smaller angular distance to the updated target direction than a direction associated with a previously selected directional transfer function pair.

6. The method of claim 1, further comprising transitioning from a previously selected directional transfer function pair to the closer matching directional transfer function pair using a crossfade.

7. The method of claim 1, further comprising interpolating between a previously selected directional transfer function pair and the closer matching directional transfer function pair.

8. The method of claim 1, wherein the updated target direction is determined based on a change in listener head orientation.

9. The method of claim 1, wherein the updated target direction is determined based on a change in a position of an ambient audio source in a virtual environment.

10. The method of claim 1, wherein different ambient audio signals of the plurality of ambient audio signals are processed concurrently using different respective directional transfer function pairs.

11. The method of claim 1, wherein rendering the output spatial audio signal comprises summing binaural signals generated by applying the selected directional transfer function pairs to corresponding ambient audio signals.

12. The method of claim 1, wherein the ambient audio signals comprise diffuse ambience components derived from an input audio scene.

13. The method of claim 1, wherein selecting the first directional transfer function pair and selecting the second directional transfer function pair are performed independently for the first and second ambient audio signals.

14. The method of claim 1, wherein the directional transfer function pairs comprise binaural room impulse response pairs.

15. The method of claim 1, wherein the closer matching directional transfer function pair is selected using a perceptual matching metric.

---

## Example Apparatus Claim

16. An apparatus for rendering spatial audio, comprising:  
   one or more processors; and  
   one or more non-transitory computer-readable media storing instructions that, when executed by the one or more processors, cause the apparatus to:  
   receive a plurality of ambient audio signals;  
   determine respective target directions for the plurality of ambient audio signals;  
   select, for the plurality of ambient audio signals, respective directional transfer function pairs from a set of directional transfer function pairs, wherein at least two of the ambient audio signals are processed using different directional transfer function pairs;  
   process the at least two ambient audio signals using the different directional transfer function pairs;  
   determine an updated target direction for one of the at least two ambient audio signals;  
   select, based on the updated target direction, a closer matching directional transfer function pair from the set of directional transfer function pairs; and  
   generate a spatial audio output using the closer matching directional transfer function pair.

---

## Example Computer-Readable Medium Claim

17. A non-transitory computer-readable storage medium storing instructions that, when executed by one or more processors, cause the one or more processors to perform operations comprising:  
   assigning different ambient audio signals to different target directions;  
   selecting different directional transfer function pairs corresponding to the different target directions;  
   filtering the different ambient audio signals using the different directional transfer function pairs;  
   updating a target direction assigned to one of the different ambient audio signals;  
   identifying, after updating the target direction, a directional transfer function pair having an associated direction that more closely matches the updated target direction than a previously used directional transfer function pair; and  
   rendering spatial audio using the identified directional transfer function pair.

---

## Additional Optional Claim Language

18. The method of claim 1, wherein selecting the closer matching directional transfer function pair comprises selecting a head-related transfer function pair associated with an azimuth and elevation nearest to an azimuth and elevation of the updated target direction.

19. The method of claim 1, wherein the closer matching directional transfer function pair is selected only when a difference between the updated target direction and a direction associated with a previously selected directional transfer function pair exceeds a threshold.

20. The method of claim 1, wherein the output spatial audio signal comprises a binaural signal for headphone playback.

21. The method of claim 1, wherein the output spatial audio signal comprises a multichannel loudspeaker signal.

22. The method of claim 1, further comprising applying gain, delay, decorrelation, reverberation, or diffusion processing to at least one of the ambient audio signals before or after processing using a selected directional transfer function pair.

23. The method of claim 1, wherein the plurality of ambient audio signals are distributed across a plurality of spatial regions, and wherein a respective directional transfer function pair is selected for each spatial region.

24. The apparatus of claim 16, wherein the instructions further cause the apparatus to smooth changes in the selected directional transfer function pairs over time to reduce discontinuities in the spatial audio output.

25. The method of claim 1, wherein the first and second target directions are selected to spatially distribute ambient energy around a listener.
